title: ECMWF runs its own AI weather model as a daily operational forecast

items.meta_description: ECMWF has taken the Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System (AIFS) into operations today, 25 February 2025, to run side by side with its traditional physics-based Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) to advance numerical weather prediction.
passages: 25 February 2025 ECMWF has taken the Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System (AIFS) into operations today, 25 February 2025, to run side by side with its traditional physics-based Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) to advance numerical weather prediction.
First operational open AI model The AIFS is the first fully operational weather prediction open model using machine learning with the widest range of parameters.

ECMWF’s Director of Forecasts and Services, Florian Pappenberger, added: “We see the AIFS and IFS as complementary, and part of providing a range of products to our user community, who decide what best suits their needs.
The first operational version is called AIFS Single.
However, ECMWF is pushing this model to create a collection of 50 different forecasts with slight variations at any given time to provide the full range of possible scenarios.
Future plans The launch of AIFS Single as an operational service is only the beginning.

items.meta_description: Abstract page for arXiv paper 2406.01465: AIFS -- ECMWF's data-driven forecasting system
passages: Here, we introduce the Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System (AIFS), a data driven forecast model developed by the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF).
AIFS is run four times daily alongside ECMWF's physics-based NWP model and forecasts are available to the public under ECMWF's open data policy.

AIFS is based on a graph neural network (GNN) encoder and decoder, and a sliding window transformer processor, and is trained on ECMWF's ERA5 re-analysis and ECMWF's operational numerical weather prediction (NWP) analyses.
We show that AIFS produces highly skilled forecasts for upper-air variables, surface weather parameters and tropical cyclone tracks.
AIFS forecast skill is assessed by comparing its forecasts to NWP analyses and direct observational data.
Machine learning-based weather forecasting models have quickly emerged as a promising methodology for accurate medium-range global weather forecasting.

items.meta_description: Abstract page for arXiv paper 2307.10128: The rise of data-driven weather forecasting
passages: Here, we compare for the first time ML-generated forecasts with standard NWP-based forecasts in an operational-like context, initialized from the same initial conditions.
Data-driven modeling based on machine learning (ML) is showing enormous potential for weather forecasting.
The uptake of ML methods could be a game-changer for the incremental progress in traditional numerical weather prediction (NWP) known as the 'quiet revolution' of weather forecasting.

An emerging new generation of ML models, developed using high-quality reanalysis datasets like ERA5 for training, allow forecasts that require much lower computational costs and that are highly-competitive in terms of accuracy.
Increasing forecast smoothness and bias drift with forecast lead time are identified as current drawbacks of ML-based forecasts.
A new NWP paradigm is emerging relying on inference from ML models and state-of-the-art analysis and reanalysis datasets for forecast initialization and model training.
